text.k055: From the request to the number ringing on AzuPhone
text.k056: Number portability is a subscriber right in Brazil: you change provider and keep the number. Azuton files the request with the carrier that currently holds the line — you do not have to negotiate anything with them.

text.k098: Will I lose my number when I move to a cloud PBX?
text.k099: No. Number portability exists precisely for this: you change provider and take the number with you. Your customers keep calling the same number, which now rings on AzuPhone extensions.
text.k100: Are virtual PBX and cloud PBX the same thing?
text.k101: Yes, they are two names for the same thing. Virtual PBX, cloud PBX and IP PBX all describe a phone system that runs over the internet, in a data centre, instead of a physical box inside the company. AzuPhone is Azuton's virtual PBX — and it is where the ported number starts ringing.
text.k102: Will my service go down during the porting?
text.k103: It does not have to. The cloud extensions are configured and tested before the switch, so the structure is ready when the number changes carrier. The switching window is agreed with you.
text.k104: Can I port more than one number?
text.k105: Yes. If your company has several numbers, or number blocks from different branches, tell us when you get in touch — the request is built for the whole set, not one at a time.
text.k106: Why might my porting request be rejected?
text.k107: The most common reason is a registration mismatch: the name, tax ID or address given here does not match what the current carrier has on file. That is why we check everything before filing. Outstanding balances with the donor carrier can also block the process.
text.k108: Do I need to notify my current carrier first?
text.k109: No. The porting request is filed by the carrier receiving the number — in this case Azuton. You do not have to negotiate your exit or ask the current carrier for release.
